main_body: Flat paving/brick floor patch of beige-grey stone slabs separated by darker mortar lines, laid in a running-bond pattern. It is a ground tile, not a standing object.
top_band: none; the ground surface is a flat plan view of slabs with no separate top band and front face
evidence: Terrain ground paving is viewed from above as a flat surface, which suits a ground tile. The slabs are separated by mortar lines with only a small highlight at each slab's top edge. There is no standing volume, so the 3/4 top and front structure does not apply. This is an acceptable ground tile for the terrain kind.

style.evidence: Each slab is a large flat fill of one beige-grey, well over 5x5 px, with no grain, speckle or per-stone shading. The only variation is a 1-row highlight at the top of each slab, a few darker dots in the corners and the mortar lines. That comes to about 3-4 tones in total. The paving reference has stones shaded one by one with highlight edges, so this looks much thinner and flatter. The mortar lines are a tinted dark taupe rather than black, which is fine, but the repeated identical slab pattern and very low per-tile colour count make it clearly poorer than the reference.
